findings.area: read side / SQL filter inside the fixed function
findings.claim: The read side no longer crashes on malformed shared-column content: malformed content becomes the named state metadata_problem='unreadable_metadata' + metadata_status='blocked' (package doc section 7; commit message; the case name '..._never_a_crash').
findings.counter_evidence: query_filing_candidates STILL raises for the same malformed values, in the same function, whenever the documented fiscal_year parameter is used, because the SQL json_extract runs before the new Python guard. The filter is built at service.py:319-327 ('AND (json_extract(d.metadata_json, \'$.acquisition.fiscal_year\') = ? OR json_extract(d.metadata_json, \'$.dayu_meta.fiscal_year\') = ?)'), the guarded parse is only reached later at service.py:399-402. Measured on the fixed tree (%TEMP%\b05probe\probe_fiscal.py, single-document TEMP catalog, PYTHONPATH=<copy of 74ffeeb>\src): for metadata_json='{not json' -> kwargs={} returns [('...', 'blocked', 'unreadable_metadata')] but kwargs={'fiscal_year': 2025} raises sqlite3.OperationalError: malformed JSON; for metadata_json='' (the state the same commit declares 'no metadata, not malformed', mapped to ok) -> kwargs={} returns [('...', 'ok', None)] but kwargs={'fiscal_year': 2025} ALSO raises sqlite3.OperationalError: malformed JSON (traceback tail: 'return list(self._connection.execute(sql, tuple(params)).fetchall())'). The new case never passes fiscal_year, so it cannot see this; the pre-existing case test_r4b05_container_shape_survives_so_json_extract_still_filters (line 680-682) shows fiscal_year is a supported, exercised path of this very method, and the SQL is byte-identical in 56f5b96 (git show 56f5b96:...service.py contains the same json_extract clause), i.e. pre-existing and untouched.
findings.required_fix: Make the filter tolerant of unreadable values, e.g. prefix it with json_valid(d.metadata_json) ('AND json_valid(d.metadata_json) AND (json_extract(...) = ? OR ...)'), or catch sqlite3.OperationalError around the fetchall and fall back to the unfiltered slice for the affected rows; then run every MALFORMED_SHARED_COLUMNS shape through query_filing_candidates both with and without fiscal_year in the same case.
findings.residual: No in-package production caller passes fiscal_year today (resolver.py:1312 passes only document_kind / source_statuses=('active',) / limit=1000, so the resolve/envelope path does not hit this), and neither filing-fetch nor revenue-forecast calls query_filing_candidates at all (grep over both repos and the filing-fetch skill: only the run directory's own probe scripts match). Reachability therefore runs through the method's public parameter surface, which the package's own claim names verbatim ('the READ side'), and through the 'invalid JSON' shape the package lists as reachable.

findings.area: read side + B06 side / exception class not covered by the guard
findings.claim: Malformed shared-column content is a named blocked state and never a crash (case name test_r4b05_malformed_shared_column_is_blocked_never_a_crash; package doc section 4 acceptance 'for every malformed shape: no exception'; section 7 'malformed content is now a named state instead of a process failure').
findings.counter_evidence: json.loads can also raise RecursionError, which is a RuntimeError and therefore NOT caught by the new 'except (TypeError, ValueError)' guards. With metadata_json = '[' * 5000 + ']' * 5000 (10 KB) the fixed tree raises: service.py:400 in query_filing_candidates -> RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded while decoding a JSON array from a unicode string; resolver.py:816 in _metadata_conflict_reason -> the same RecursionError, so build_resolution_envelope also fails (tracebacks captured by %TEMP%\b05probe\probe_tb.py). Depth 1000 is still fine (it parses, is not a dict, and is correctly reported as unreadable_metadata), so the boundary lies between 1000 and 5000 nesting levels on this CPython 3.13.9 with the default recursion limit. Object nesting ('{"a":' * 5000 ...) fails the same way. The claim as worded ('never a crash', 'every shape') is therefore literally false.
findings.required_fix: Catch the parser's full failure surface at both sites - 'except Exception' (or at least '(TypeError, ValueError, RecursionError)') - and add one malformed case with a deeply nested payload; alternatively reject payloads above a size/depth budget before parsing.
findings.residual: I did not demonstrate any in-package writer producing >= 2000 nesting depth; the value is reachable through any caller that writes the column, which the package's own test helper _corrupt_metadata treats as legitimate input ('a caller-visible malformed shape is a legitimate input to test'). Under a strict reading of the severity rubric this is P0 ('the read path can still crash'); I graded it P1 because the input is synthetic and every realistic writer-produced shape is covered.

findings.area: envelope read path / unaudited parse site
findings.claim: The B06 side now returns a reason for malformed content 'so the envelope blocks, agreeing with the read side' (commit message); 'the two sides say the same thing' (package doc section 7); the residual lists the unaudited json.loads(metadata_json) sites.
findings.counter_evidence: The envelope still crashes on the same malformed column, through a parse site that is neither changed nor listed: prompt_injection.read_prompt_injection_review (prompt_injection.py:148 'metadata = json.loads(row[0] or "{}")', guarded only by 'except json.JSONDecodeError' at line 159) is called from build_resolution_envelope at resolver.py:1014, i.e. BEFORE _metadata_conflict_reason at resolver.py:1036. Measured (%TEMP%\b05probe\probe_tb.py): with metadata_json stored as GBK bytes (b'{"title": "\u516c\u53f8"}' - SQLite stores a non-UTF-8 BLOB in the TEXT column and returns bytes), the read side answers blocked/unreadable_metadata while build_resolution_envelope raises UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xb9 in position 11 (resolver.py:1014 -> prompt_injection.py:148). The same site also propagates RecursionError for deep nesting. So for that shape the two sides still disagree about the same document - the exact defect state the package claims to have closed - and the commit's residual list (artifact_backfill, artifact_read_model, backfill_v2, extraction_quality, llm_summarizer, migration_ledger) does not contain prompt_injection.py at all. Note the pre-fix tree crashed for this shape too (read side UnicodeDecodeError), so this commit converted 'both sides crash' into 'read side blocked, envelope crashes' rather than into agreement.
findings.required_fix: Guard prompt_injection.py:148 (and the write-side sibling at line 108) with the same policy as the two changed sites, or route every documents.metadata_json read through one shared guarded helper; extend the residual list in section 6/section 7 and the commit's residual paragraph to name prompt_injection.py, and add a malformed-shape case that builds a real envelope from a real catalog with a non-UTF-8/byte value.
findings.residual: Requires a value that JSONDecodeError does not cover (bytes / non-UTF-8 BLOB, or deep nesting). The B06 review fuzzed _metadata_conflict_reason directly with bytes and saw no exception (its claim 5), which is correct for that function in isolation but does not cover the envelope built from a real catalog - the divergence I measured is in a different function on the same call.
